authority: Owner decision 2026-10-22 about 15:30 EDT: keep typed choice scoring, run a head-to-head benchmark before further packaging; the owner chooses the workload from the results. No npm publication.

workload.task: Three-way GitHub issue routing (bug, feature, question); the application suggests, a human decides
workload.data: NLBSE'24 issue report classification, revision 2927bc67, CSV SHA-256 pins in examples/issue-triage/dataset.js
workload.test: 150 test issues: stratifiedSample(test, perCell 10, seed issue-triage-20261021), as in reports/issue-triage-comparison-20261022
workload.train: 90 train issues: stratifiedSample(train, perCell 6, seed issue-triage-20261021); used only for label-free centering and for choosing the best open alternative
workload.state: documentText(issue, 1600) from examples/issue-triage/triage.js for every engine; reranker lanes fall back to 800 then 300 characters only when the prompt reaches maxSeqLen 1024
workload.issueText: never committed; results record indices, labels, probabilities and timings

a-runtime-parity.question: Same model, same weights and same precision: how do Doppler and Transformers.js differ in accuracy, numerical agreement, latency and memory?
a-runtime-parity.model: Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B@e61197ed, application prompts and yes/no answer logits

lanes.doppler-f16: Doppler compat load() of a fresh standard-BLAKE3 F16 conversion from the pinned source safetensors; F16 weights. Activation precision recorded exactly: f16 if the af16 runtime lane runs this model correctly, otherwise f32 and the mismatch stated
lanes.transformersjs-fp16: Transformers.js 4.3.1, device webgpu, dtype fp16 (model_fp16 graph of the export already used in reports/issue-triage-comparison-20261022, plus the source generation_config.json)

a-runtime-parity.numericalReference: FP32 ONNX of the same checkpoint on CPU (reports/issue-triage-numerics-20261022/fp32-oracle.js) on the 40-issue subset

b-product.question: Doppler with its chosen model versus the best open alternative, each used as its authors intend

lanes.doppler-capsule-q4k: Doppler 0.6.32 candidate archive 3f87f551 and test-signed Capsule ...-92b23b6a7b37aa70 (Q4K reranker successor 6beadee3), installed into OPFS through the application's installation adapter
lanes.open-jev-kev-0.6b: open-jev 0.1.2 + Transformers.js 4.3.1, model onnx-community/kev-0.6b-ONNX@5a827091, dtype chosen by open-jev (q4f16 on WebGPU with shader-f16, q4 otherwise)

b-product.openJevQuestion: choice("What type of GitHub issue is this?", ["bug", "feature", "question"], descriptions = the three TRIAGE_POLICY route queries); default temperature and truncation
b-product.bestOpenAlternative: the open-jev lane with the highest train-split accuracy; all open-jev lanes are reported

notRun.TypeSafe Jev: hosted, paid API with new signups paused; would send issue text to a third party; not run without an owner-provided account and approval
notRun.Chrome Decisions API: explainer only, dev-trial flag code from 2026-10; recorded as unavailable unless chrome://flags#decisions-api exists in the tested Chrome build
notRun.Laya builds: kevala, @r4ai/laya-web and open-jev-laya use other wrappers and checkpoints; not in this run

metrics.accuracy: test accuracy and macro-F1 of the top choice; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 20261022) of differences against doppler-capsule-q4k (product) and between parity lanes
metrics.calibration: three-way probabilities: open-jev probabilities as returned; reranker lanes softmax over route scores yes-no at temperature 1 (raw, the primary) and after label-free centering with train-split offsets. Report ECE (10 equal-width bins of top-choice confidence), multiclass Brier score and NLL
metrics.coldComplete: fresh browser profile, empty caches, model files from a local byte-counting HTTP origin: page navigation to first decision returned; 3 repetitions per lane, lanes alternated
metrics.warmComplete: per-decision wall time from request to probabilities, all test decisions after the first; median and p90
metrics.memory: peak total browser RSS over all processes of the profile (Linux /proc; macOS ps), and amdgpu GTT+VRAM on Linux; sampled every 200 ms
metrics.gpuProvider: WebGPU adapter info (vendor, architecture, device, description) and adapter features as seen by the page; the engine's own report of its device/dtype/execution provider; console warnings about nodes assigned to CPU
metrics.cpuFallback: the same page with navigator.gpu removed before any engine loads: record what each lane does (explicit failure, or the device and dtype it falls back to) and, where it runs, accuracy and warm latency on the first 30 test issues

platforms.amd-host: Linux 7.0.0-38, Radeon 8060S (RADV STRIX_HALO): Google Chrome stable 146.0.7680.177 (Vulkan); Firefox Nightly (WebGPU is Nightly-only on Linux), exact build recorded; Node 22.22.1 (Doppler via webgpu@0.4.0 Dawn, Transformers.js via onnxruntime-node)
platforms.mars: Apple M3, macOS: Safari, Chrome stable, Firefox; Node. Run by the mac-host owner with the same harness

fairness.sameState: every lane sees the same issue text and truncation budget
fairness.noTestTuning: prompts, questions and centering are fixed here; the test split is never used to choose anything
fairness.oneEngineAtATime: lanes run one at a time on an otherwise idle GPU; other GPU clients recorded from amdgpu fdinfo before and after
fairness.determinism: accuracy is computed from the first repetition; later repetitions must reproduce its first 10 decisions or the lane is reported as nondeterministic

decisionRule: No promotion or claim follows automatically. The owner chooses the workload from the results.
